lines: This is a spreadsheet with detailed paddle information that ThePickleballStudio has tested.

There are several view options in this spreadsheet that you can see below. This is to help you narrow down the long list of information into things that you are looking for quicker. One note, if a view is using “sort by group” this doesn’t load all the groups in one page. Once you get to the bottom you’ll see “show more groups” click this and you’ll see more.

The great thing about this spreadsheet is on the right side you have “filter” and “sort” where you can create your own filters and view options if you want to see something more specific than what I’ve already specified.

RPM stands for revolutions per minute. I came up with a testing method to roughly estimate the spin potential of a paddle. This test is not perfect but I have found it to be a reliable test to determine whether plays at high spin levels or not. What I have found is that you need to look at paddles in a low tier, average tier, and high tier for spin. Anything <1200 is low tier. 1200-1400 is average tier and 1500+ is a high tier for spin. So don’t get caught up in what paddle is ranked 1-5. Usually at that point they are all fantastic for spin and the individual rank doesn’t matter nearly as much as knowing whether it’s a high tier or low tier spin paddle. Also know that paddles may get varying amounts of spin depending on you as a player. Some players may need a head light paddle to generate more head speed, others might need lighter weight, a longer or shorter handle, etc. This is simply meant to give you an estimate of the spin potential you can expect.
Swing weight can be very helpful for determining how much harder a paddle may be to swing than what you’re used to. Here are some reference numbers:
<100 VERY low swing weight and the paddle will feel extremely fast in hand
100-110 still very fast in the hand and where most square paddle shapes average
110-120 is where a lot of elongated paddles average. Once you pass about 115, that’s when you may start to notice a small compromise in hand speed.
120+ These paddle will feel quite slow in the hand.

Use the spreadsheet to see the swing weight of your paddle and get a reference point of how much easier or harder a new one will be to swing. Most people tend to notice a big difference in paddle swing weights when the number changes by 10 points. Example: 110 vs 120.
